title: fix(react): emit `BaseSchema.testId` as `data-testid` (objectui#8268)
body:
Fixes #8268

`BaseSchema.testId`'s JSDoc promised *"Rendered as data-testid attribute."* Nothing rendered
it. The key was absent from `SchemaRenderer`'s metadata destructure, so it fell through into
the spread, was handed to the component as a React prop, and reached the DOM under React's
fallback spelling for an unrecognised prop — a non-standard lowercase `testid` that
`screen.getByTestId(...)` and `[data-testid=...]` both miss. The zod mirror accepts the key, so
the author got no parse-time warning either.

## The measurement

Reproduced on my base `93127bd6f` through the **real** `ui:scroll-area` renderer, node
`{ id: 'my-scroll', testId: 'my-tid' }`, both worlds on the same probe:

| | `[data-testid="my-tid"]` | `[testid="my-tid"]` | contrast leg: `id` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | **false** | **true** | `id="my-scroll"` + `data-obj-id="my-scroll"` — **present** |
| after | **true** | **false** | `id="my-scroll"` + `data-obj-id="my-scroll"` — **present** |

Root attributes, before and after:

```
before  dir="ltr" class="relative overflow-hidden" style="..." id="my-scroll" testid="my-tid" data-obj-id="my-scroll" data-obj-type="ui:scroll-area"
after   dir="ltr" class="relative overflow-hidden" style="..." id="my-scroll" data-testid="my-tid" data-obj-id="my-scroll" data-obj-type="ui:scroll-area"
```

The `id` leg is the **firing positive control on the same run**: the strip list and the spread
work as designed, and only this key had no mapping. It is deliberately green in both worlds,
and the source comment on it names the wrong fix it guards against — stopping the leak by
widening the strip list mechanically and sweeping `id` (or the `data-obj-*` pair emitted from
the same place) out with it.

Two things the card did not have, measured here:

- **React's own dev warning does fire** — and makes it worse. It tells the author to
  *"spell it as lowercase `testid`"*, i.e. steers them to the attribute that does not work,
  further from the documented one.
- **objectui#4795's unevaluated-expression diagnostic did report `testId`** before this change
  (measured: an authored `testId: '${data.x}'` was named in its output), because the key was in
  `componentProps`. The strip list is that diagnostic's exclusion list, so stripping the key
  would have silently narrowed its coverage. `testId` holds a literal, not predicate source, so
  it is stripped from the spread and **kept in the scan set**; a case pins that.

## Branch A, and why I departed from objectui#7088

objectui#7088 — the class-mirror, `BaseSchema.hidden` — resolved by **fixing the declaration and
declining the renderer change** (director ruling 2026-09-01, maintainer 「同意」; 「分化不做」,
Clause-② `no`). That is branch B, and it is the strong prior. I took **A**, and the ruling's own
reasoning is why.

#7088 declined the renderer change because it was *「发布 prop 上的行为变更,零具名消费者」* — a
behaviour change on a published prop with **zero named consumers**. That premise does not hold
here. Measured on this base, the promise already has carriers outside the type declaration:

- `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` states it as a table row — *"Test identifier, rendered
  as `data-testid`."* — **and authors `testId` in that page's own base-schema example.**
- `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` — `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` identifies a file as an
  ObjectUI schema node **by this key**, in a published CLI, with a comment saying the set
  "grows only when `BaseSchema` grows".
- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` — `ObjectGridSlotKey` and `ObjectFormSlotKey` both pin it.
- `packages/core` — `SchemaBuilder.testId()` is a published builder method that writes it.
- Two example suites declare it a key "the render pipeline handles for EVERY node".
- 15 component doc pages carry the row. (The card said 16; that count has drifted —
  `layout/box.mdx` still carries a `// Base properties` block, so the **16** for that grep is
  intact, but its block was trimmed to `id` / `visible` and no longer lists `testId`.)
- **ADR-0054 C4 — shipped, all five phases** — reads *"The renderer emits `data-testid` … derived
  from metadata"*. Retiring the key is a move against a landed ADR.

Two more asymmetries against B:

1. **The second carrier is fenced.** The promise's most author-facing copy lives in
   `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, which this PR is fenced off (objectui#8914 is in
   flight there). Under B that page keeps a live falsehood this PR cannot fix; under A it
   becomes true with **no doc edit at all**.
2. **`hidden` had a behaviour to describe; this key has none.** "Make the declaration honest"
   here means describing nothing, which is retirement — and retirement crosses `types` (decl +
   zod mirror + two pinned key unions), `core` (a published builder method), `cli` (a published
   marker list), 15 doc pages and the fenced file, for a p3 finding.

ADR-0049 is *enforce-**or**-remove*; this is the enforce arm. AGENTS.md #0.1 is not in tension:
there is no lenient fallback, no alias, no `??`-default here — the key is `BaseSchema`'s own
declaration and it is honoured under its own single spelling.

Triage's **third determinate defect** (the stray lowercase `testid` reaching the DOM whatever is
decided about the promise) is **subsumed**: the key is now in the strip list.

## The one thing that had to be measured, not reasoned

The emission is spread **conditionally**:

```ts
...(_testId === undefined ? {} : { 'data-testid': _testId }),
```

The unconditional `'data-testid': _testId` form was written first and turned **9 tests red
across 5 files**, three of them the byte-for-byte props-bag pins (objectui#6708 / #6752 /
#6760). Passing `undefined` is invisible in rendered HTML but puts the key in every node's props
bag, and a component that sets its own `data-testid` before spreading what it is handed — the
ADR-0054 C4 shape, common here — has its locator overwritten with `undefined` and loses it. A
node that authors no `testId` is now byte-identical to before this PR, and two cases pin both
sides of that precedence.

## Verification

Everything below at `94326f2dd` unless stated.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/src packages/types/src` → **`Test Files 238 passed (238) · Tests 4084 passed (4084)`**
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src packages/app-shell/src` → **`Test Files 925 passed (925) · Tests 8825 passed, 1 skipped (8826)`** (the published-face consumers)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/react run type-check` → both `Done`. Coverage of the new file proved, not assumed: `tsc -p packages/react/tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists `SchemaRenderer.testIdEmission.test.tsx`.
- `turbo run lint --filter=@object-ui/react --filter=@object-ui/types` → `Tasks: 3 successful, 3 total`, **0 errors**. Warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any`; none falls on an edited line (SchemaRenderer.tsx warnings stop at 1440, edits are 1477+; no base.ts warning in 415–460; none on the new file).
- `pnpm changeset:check` → 3 assertions pass · `pnpm check:control-bytes` → `OK (scanned 7113 tracked text file(s))` · `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers` → OK · `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` → OK · `pnpm check:doc-types` → `Every documented component type is registered.` · `pnpm check:doc-fences` → OK
- Self-scan beyond the gate: `grep -naP` for control bytes over all four diff files → **0** each, with a proven-positive probe.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test THE-FOUR-PATHS` → `NOT GOVERNED`.

**Ablation — the pin can actually fail, twice, and the control survives both.** Run on the
committed implementation, each leg with its on-disk mutation proved by blob hash and restored
with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` under a `trap`, restore proved by an empty `git diff HEAD`
and by the blob returning to `90426f2740737ede85a4ed871b899822ab9b3fd3`:

| leg | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | delete the `data-testid` emission | `Tests 2 failed · 4 passed (6)` |
| B | put `testId` back in the spread (re-create the leak) | `Tests 1 failed · 5 passed (6)` — the "NOT the lowercase spelling" case |

The `id` control was green in all four worlds.

`pnpm check:doc-snippets` and `pnpm check:doc-examples` first returned **exit 2 =
PREREQUISITE NOT MET**, which is neither red nor green. Rather than report that, the
prerequisite was satisfied — `turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs
--build-filter) --concurrency=2` → `Tasks: 35 successful, 35 total` — and both re-run to a real
verdict:

- `pnpm check:doc-snippets` → exit 0, `Semantic phase: 638 of 638 block(s) judged, 0 failed.`
- `pnpm check:doc-examples` → exit 0, `Every covered @example compiles, or fails exactly as its ledger row declares.`

Consistent with the independent argument that they could not move: their population is
TypeScript fences in documents, this diff changes **0** document files, and
`packages/types/src/base.ts`'s diff is **comment-only** — every changed line in it is a JSDoc
line, verified with a probe whose positive control finds the non-comment changed lines in
`SchemaRenderer.tsx`. No declaration byte moved.

## 验收备注 — measured, deliberately not fixed

- `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` line ~90 carries the promise as a table row and line
  ~61 authors `testId` in the base-schema example. **Both become correct with this PR and no
  edit** — which is the point — but the file is fenced (objectui#8914). Flagged, not touched.
- The two example suites' `PIPELINE_KEYS` lists (`examples/schema-catalog/test/`) call `testId`
  "a key the render pipeline handles for EVERY node". That was false before this PR and is true
  after it. No edit needed; noted so the next reader knows it was checked, not missed.
- Triage's p2 re-grade condition — `testId` authored in a live schema node — is **not met**:
  the only authored occurrence in the tree is the doc JSON example above. Left at p3.

## Clause-②

`Clause-②: yes`, declared on the card's claim comment and carried here. Both branches move a
published face and this one moves the renderer's DOM output on nodes that author `testId` — in
both directions, since the accidental `[testid=…]` stops matching. The A-vs-B call itself is the
contract-face question the carrier exists for, and this PR is the reviewable increment it is
supposed to go up with.
